Router calls the chain kept, in the selected window.

panels.title: Trades (settled)

panels.description: Share of indexed calls where both the transaction and the router call succeeded.

panels.title: Call success rate

panels.description:
Router fee plus client fee.

Captured positive slippage is part of router_fee_amount, not a separate stream: with positive-slippage capture enabled the surplus is paid to the router fee receiver, and fees_taken confirms the on-chain transfer equals the whole router_fee_amount. So totals here are router fee plus client fee only. Adding positive slippage on top would double-count it -- on robinhood, where the output fee is 0 bps and the router fee is therefore entirely slippage, that mistake doubles the figure.

USD covers trades the pricer has stamped; see Priced coverage and the pricing-source table. Unpriced trades contribute nothing, so read totals as a floor.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sum((coalesce(router_fee_amount, 0) + coalesce(client_fee_amount, 0)) / power(10, decimals_out) * price_out_usd) AS total_captured_usd
FROM trades_settled
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring}) AND price_out_usd IS NOT NULL AND decimals_out IS NOT NULL

panels.title: Priced coverage

panels.description: Indexed router calls per interval, stacked by chain so the bar height is total throughput and the segments are its composition. Bucket width follows the dashboard interval, so it changes with the selected range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(block_time, $__interval), chain AS metric, count(*) AS trades
FROM trades
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})

panels.title: Trades per interval by chain

panels.description:
Share of router calls per interval that reverted, on a fixed 0-100% axis so spikes are comparable between chains and over time. Dashed guides mark 5% and 20%, and the area above each is shaded, so a chain crossing into trouble is visible without reading values. The legend gives each chain's worst and mean bucket for the range.

Buckets with fewer than 5 calls are dropped: one failed call out of one reads as 100% and was what made this chart unreadable. Absolute failure counts, and the reasons, are in Top revert selectors.

These are TychoRouter calls (v2, v3_0, v3_1 are the only router_versions present), so a revert here is an ordinary swap failure -- slippage, insufficient output, a token refusing the transfer.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(block_time, $__interval), chain AS metric,
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success) / count(*) AS call_failure_pct
FROM trades
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING count(*) >= 5
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Call failure rate by chain

panels.description:
Every configured sink, taken from the cursors_<chain> tables, so a chain that has never recorded a trade is still listed with trades_total 0 -- the case a query over `trades` alone cannot show. Ignores the dashboard time range and the chain variable on purpose: this panel answers 'is any sink not producing', which filtering would hide.

Read cursor_block against last_trade: a cursor far ahead of the last trade with blocks_since_last_trade near 0 means the sink is mid-backfill, not stuck. A cursor of 0 means nothing was ever ingested.

probes are calls the chain discarded (state_committed false) -- a caller quoting the router by calling it and reverting. They are real router calls but not trades, and every volume and fee panel excludes them. unflagged are rows indexed before state_committed existed; they also stay out of the settled figures, and a re-index clears them.

The chain list here is a literal union and does not pick up a new chain on its own: plasma is configured in the substreams package but has no cursors_plasma table yet, and needs a line added here once its sink runs. The chain variable above is derived from the table list and will show it immediately.

targets.rawSql:
WITH c AS (
            SELECT 'arbitrum'  AS chain, max(block_num) AS cursor_block FROM cursors_arbitrum
  UNION ALL SELECT 'base',      max(block_num) FROM cursors_base
  UNION ALL SELECT 'bsc',       max(block_num) FROM cursors_bsc
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ethereum',  max(block_num) FROM cursors_ethereum
  UNION ALL SELECT 'polygon',   max(block_num) FROM cursors_polygon
  UNION ALL SELECT 'robinhood', max(block_num) FROM cursors_robinhood
  UNION ALL SELECT 'unichain',  max(block_num) FROM cursors_unichain
), t AS (
  SELECT chain,
         count(*) AS trades_total,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE state_committed) AS settled,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE state_committed IS FALSE) AS probes,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE state_committed IS NULL) AS unflagged,
         max(block_number) AS last_trade_block,
         max(block_time) AS last_trade
  FROM trades
  GROUP BY chain
)
SELECT c.chain,
       c.cursor_block,
       coalesce(t.trades_total, 0) AS trades_total,
       coalesce(t.settled, 0) AS settled,
       coalesce(t.probes, 0) AS probes,
       coalesce(t.unflagged, 0) AS unflagged,
       t.last_trade,
       c.cursor_block - t.last_trade_block AS blocks_since_last_trade
FROM c
  LEFT JOIN t ON t.chain = c.chain
ORDER BY trades_total, c.chain

panels.title: Sinks and chain coverage

panels.description:
Share of router calls that reverted, one line per integrator watermark, so a bad watermarked flow is visible next to the rest instead of hidden inside it. The watermark is stored hex-encoded and decoded here; calls with no tag group as '(untagged)'.

Each point is a trailing 6-hour rate, not the rate of its own bucket. A watermarked flow is a small slice of the calls -- on ethereum it has run at about 3 to 4 calls an hour -- so a per-bucket rate is either dropped for want of calls or swings between 0% and 100% on a single revert. The trailing window holds tens of calls behind every point at any zoom level, so the line stays continuous and readable. A point whose window holds fewer than 5 calls is dropped, which trims the left edge of the range until the window has filled.

The axis starts at 0% and grows from 10%, rather than the fixed 0-100% of Call failure rate by chain: the difference worth seeing here is a few percent against a few tenths of a percent. Dashed guides mark 5% and 20%.

Which calls revert, and why, is in Reverts by watermark and chain.

A watermark can carry an ERC-8021 builder-code suffix after the fynd tag: the last 16 bytes are the 0x8021 marker, then a schema byte, then a length byte, then the builder code. It is stripped here so a tagged trade counts under its fynd watermark rather than as its own series -- without that, 'propeller' and 'propeller + a builder code' were counted as two different integrators. The code itself is broken out in Volume and fees by builder code.

A fynd watermark can also carry 16 per-request bytes after the `fynd/<version>/<id>` tag. They are dropped, so every trade from one deployment counts under one tag.

targets.rawSql:
WITH bucket AS (
  SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(block_time, $__interval),
         CASE
         WHEN coalesce(watermark, '') = '' THEN '(untagged)'
         WHEN watermark !~* '^0x([0-9a-f]{2})+$' THEN watermark
         WHEN left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) = '' THEN '(untagged)'
         WHEN left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) ~ '^(66796e642f(?:3[0-9]|2e)+2f(?:3[0-9]|6[1-6]){16})'
           THEN convert_from(decode(substring(left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) from '^(66796e642f(?:3[0-9]|2e)+2f(?:3[0-9]|6[1-6]){16})'), 'hex'), 'LATIN1')
         WHEN left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) ~ '^(2[0-9a-f]|[3-6][0-9a-f]|7[0-9a-e])+$'
           THEN convert_from(decode(left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)), 'hex'), 'LATIN1')
         ELSE '0x' || left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END))
       END AS metric,
         count(*) AS calls,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success) AS reverts
  FROM trades
  WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT "time", metric, revert_pct
FROM (
  SELECT "time", metric,
         100.0 * sum(reverts) OVER w / nullif(sum(calls) OVER w, 0) AS revert_pct,
         sum(calls) OVER w AS window_calls
  FROM bucket
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY metric ORDER BY "time" RANGE BETWEEN 21600 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
) windowed
WHERE window_calls >= 5
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Reverts by watermark and chain

panels.description:
Who the reverts belong to. One row per caller of the router, sorted by the number of reverts it produced, so the caller behind a rate spike is at the top.

Sort by the count, not by the rate: a caller with one call and one revert is at 100% and means nothing, while the caller that moves a chain is the one with hundreds. share_of_chain_reverts gives the count as a share of every revert on that chain in the range, which is the number that says whether one caller explains the chain.

eoas counts the distinct tx.origin behind the caller. A 1 there is a bot calling the router itself; a few hundred is an aggregator or a front end, and its reverts are spread over its users.

top_selector is the error selector most of the reverts carried. A selector the router does not define comes from a pool or a token -- 0xa932492f is the Solidly invariant error K(), 0x08c379a0 is the standard Error(string). Click latest_revert_tx to open the newest one in Router Trade Detail.

reason is the decoded error, which is usually what you want; the selector alone does not separate an out-of-gas from a failed callback. The arguments are cut off the name so one error does not split into a row per value, and sample_reason keeps a full example including them. A revert with no selector still carries a reason: 'out of gas' and 'execution reverted' arrive that way.

targets.rawSql:
WITH sender AS (
  SELECT chain, msg_sender,
         count(*) AS calls,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success) AS reverts,
         count(DISTINCT eoa) AS eoas,
         mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY coalesce(revert_selector, '(none)'))
           FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success) AS top_selector,
         mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY coalesce(nullif(split_part(revert_reason, '(', 1), ''), revert_reason, '(no reason)'))
           FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success) AS top_reason,
         (array_agg(tx_hash ORDER BY block_time DESC) FILTER (WHERE NOT call_success))[1]
           AS latest_revert_tx
  FROM trades
  WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT chain, msg_sender, calls, reverts,
       100.0 * reverts / calls AS revert_pct,
       100.0 * reverts / nullif(sum(reverts) OVER (PARTITION BY chain), 0)
         AS share_of_chain_reverts,
       eoas, top_selector, top_reason, latest_revert_tx
FROM sender
WHERE reverts > 0
ORDER BY reverts DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Reverts by msg.sender

panels.description:
Error selector of failed router calls. 0x08c379a0 is the standard Error(string); revert_reason is stored raw and is often not printable, so a sample transaction is given instead of decoding here.

Click a sample transaction to open it in Router Trade Detail.

reason is the decoded error, which is usually what you want; the selector alone does not separate an out-of-gas from a failed callback. The arguments are cut off the name so one error does not split into a row per value, and sample_reason keeps a full example including them. A revert with no selector still carries a reason: 'out of gas' and 'execution reverted' arrive that way.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT coalesce(revert_selector, '(none)') AS selector,
       coalesce(nullif(split_part(revert_reason, '(', 1), ''), revert_reason, '(no reason)') AS reason,
       count(*) AS failures,
       max(left(revert_reason, 120)) AS sample_reason,
       max(tx_hash) AS sample_tx
FROM trades
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND NOT call_success AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY failures DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.description:
Hop count by protocol system. One trade contributes several hops, so these totals exceed the trade count. Names are resolved at query time from the executors table through the trade_hop_protocols view -- trade_hops now stores only the executor address, so a newly deployed executor gets its name without re-indexing.

A caller can quote the router on chain by calling it and reverting; that probe returns normally and is stored as a trade, but the chain threw its state away. targets.rawSql:
SELECT ps AS protocol_system, count(*) AS hops
FROM trade_hop_protocols h
  JOIN trades_settled t ON t.id = h.trade_id
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(h.protocol_systems) AS ps
WHERE $__timeFilter(t.block_time) AND t.chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY hops DESC
LIMIT 15

panels.description:
Running sum of volume_usd per chain, drawn as a staircase: the line holds flat through intervals with no trades and steps up when volume arrives.

The y axis is log10. Ethereum currently carries about 99% of volume -- the spread between the largest and smallest chain is roughly 60,000x -- and on a linear axis every other chain sits flat on the bottom. Log makes each chain's trajectory legible at the cost of making the gaps between them look smaller than they are; the legend's totals are the figures to quote.

FROM (

  FROM trades_settled
  WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring}) AND volume_usd IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY 1, 2
) s
ORDER BY s."time"

panels.description:

panels.description:
Fees are always taken in the trade's output token (verified: every fees_taken row has token = token_out), so this is the fee mix by token.

       coalesce(pt.symbol, t.token_out) AS token,
       count(*) AS fee_rows,
       count(t.price_out_usd) AS priced_rows,
       sum(coalesce(router_fee_amount, 0) + coalesce(client_fee_amount, 0)) AS fee_raw,
       sum((coalesce(router_fee_amount, 0) + coalesce(client_fee_amount, 0)) / power(10, coalesce(t.decimals_out, pt.decimals))) AS fee_tokens,

FROM trades_settled t
  LEFT JOIN preferred_tokens pt ON pt.chain = t.chain AND lower(pt.address) = lower(t.token_out)
WHERE $__timeFilter(t.block_time) AND t.chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
  AND (coalesce(router_fee_amount, 0) + coalesce(client_fee_amount, 0)) > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY fee_usd DESC NULLS LAST, fee_raw DESC
LIMIT 30

panels.title: Fees by msg.sender

panels.description:
What each fee recipient holds in a router's ERC-6909 vault. A v3 router pays a fee by crediting its own vault rather than transferring the token out, so router revenue sits in the router until someone withdraws it -- the fee panels above measure what was credited, this measures what is still there.

balance comes from the vault_balances view, which combines the ERC-6909 Transfer events in vault_transfers with the fee credits in fees_taken; the credits emit no Transfer, so neither source alone gives a balance. A balance of zero means the owner withdrew everything and is kept so past collection stays visible. A negative balance means rows are missing -- expected while a chain still holds trades indexed before state_committed existed, and cleared by re-indexing.

balance_usd values the position at the most recent price seen for that token on that chain, which is a spot estimate rather than a mark: it is blank for a token no priced trade has produced, and token units are blank for a token whose decimals are in neither preferred_tokens nor a priced trade. Ordering falls back to the raw balance in that case.

The price lookup is a single pass over trades rather than a per-row correlated subquery, which is what made this panel take ten seconds.

targets.rawSql:
WITH vb AS (
  SELECT * FROM vault_balances
  WHERE chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
),
-- One latest USD price per (chain, token), computed once. The correlated LATERAL
-- this replaces re-ran a ~1300-row index scan per vault row: 2378 scans, 1.3M buffers.
px AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (t.chain, t.token_out)
         t.chain, t.token_out AS token, t.price_out_usd, t.decimals_out
  FROM trades t
  WHERE t.tx_success AND t.call_success AND t.state_committed
    AND t.price_out_usd IS NOT NULL
    AND t.chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
  ORDER BY t.chain, t.token_out, t.block_time DESC
)
SELECT v.chain, v.router, coalesce(pt.symbol, v.token) AS token, v.owner,
       v.balance / power(10, coalesce(pt.decimals, px.decimals_out)) AS balance_tokens,
       v.credited_as_fees / power(10, coalesce(pt.decimals, px.decimals_out)) AS credited_as_fees_tokens,
       v.balance / power(10, coalesce(pt.decimals, px.decimals_out)) * px.price_out_usd AS balance_usd,
       v.n_flows, v.last_change
FROM vb v
  LEFT JOIN preferred_tokens pt ON pt.chain = v.chain AND lower(pt.address) = lower(v.token)
  LEFT JOIN px ON px.chain = v.chain AND px.token = v.token
ORDER BY balance_usd DESC NULLS LAST, v.balance DESC
LIMIT 40

panels.title: Volume and fees by builder code

panels.description:
The table above, summed across tokens: what each owner holds in one router's vault on one chain, as a single USD figure. One row per chain, router and owner.

Only tokens the pricer has a USD rate for are summed. priced_tokens against tokens says how much of each vault that covers, and it is often well under half, so read balance_usd as a floor on the true balance rather than the whole of it. The rate is each token's most recent settled price, so this is a current-value snapshot, not a historical series.

Vaults totalling zero, or with no priced token at all, are left out.

The price lookup is a single pass over trades rather than a per-row correlated subquery, which is what made this panel take ten seconds.

targets.rawSql:
WITH vb AS (
  SELECT * FROM vault_balances
  WHERE chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
),
-- One latest USD price per (chain, token), computed once. The correlated LATERAL
-- this replaces re-ran a ~1300-row index scan per vault row: 2378 scans, 1.3M buffers.
px AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (t.chain, t.token_out)
         t.chain, t.token_out AS token, t.price_out_usd, t.decimals_out
  FROM trades t
  WHERE t.tx_success AND t.call_success AND t.state_committed
    AND t.price_out_usd IS NOT NULL
    AND t.chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
  ORDER BY t.chain, t.token_out, t.block_time DESC
)
SELECT v.chain, v.router, v.owner,
       sum(v.balance / power(10, coalesce(pt.decimals, px.decimals_out)) * px.price_out_usd) AS balance_usd,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE px.price_out_usd IS NOT NULL) AS priced_tokens,
       count(*) AS tokens,
       max(v.last_change) AS last_change
FROM vb v
  LEFT JOIN preferred_tokens pt ON pt.chain = v.chain AND lower(pt.address) = lower(v.token)
  LEFT JOIN px ON px.chain = v.chain AND px.token = v.token
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING sum(v.balance / power(10, coalesce(pt.decimals, px.decimals_out)) * px.price_out_usd) > 0
ORDER BY balance_usd DESC
LIMIT 40

panels.description:
USD volume of races we lost: transactions where the router was quoted and nothing settled.

A probe is a router call that ran and returned normally but whose state the chain threw away (tx_success and call_success, state_committed false): someone called the router inside a frame they then reverted, to read our price. That is a route race -- they asked us for a quote and compared it.

A race is a transaction in which the router was probed. A transaction that settled without a probe is not counted: nobody asked us for a price in it, so there was no race to win.     AND tx_success AND call_success AND state_committed
    AND volume_usd IS NOT NULL
    AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
    AND left(lower(substring(watermark, 3)),
             greatest(0, length(lower(substring(watermark, 3)))
               - CASE WHEN lower(substring(watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$'

                      ELSE 0 END))
        = '70726f70656c6c6572'

panels.title: Trade sizes by chain

panels.description:
Share of settled trades whose amount_out came in under expected_amount_out. The price moved between the quote and the fill, and this counts how often.

This is the finer of the two volatility measures: it is per trade, not per hour, and it is measured on the same execution path that produces the reverts.

This measure is censored, and it understates volatility exactly when volatility is highest. A fill that falls further below the quote than the caller's tolerance reverts instead of settling, so it never appears here. Read it together with the revert rate, never on its own.

How to use this with the failure charts:
- revert rate up AND this up: the market moved. The callers with the tightest slippage tolerance fail first, and there is nothing to fix in the router.
- revert rate up AND this flat: look for a bug. Read the reason column in Top revert reasons; an out-of-gas or a paused contract does not come with price movement.

The bucket has a floor of one hour. Without it the range picks a bucket of about ten minutes, and a chain that does 110 trades an hour falls under the minimum count and disappears completely. That is why ethereum was absent.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(block_time, $__interval), chain AS metric,
       100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE amount_out < expected_amount_out) / count(*) AS pct_below_quote
FROM trades
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND tx_success AND call_success AND state_committed
  AND expected_amount_out > 0 AND amount_out IS NOT NULL AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING count(*) >= 20
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Quote drift: fills below quote

panels.description:
Among the trades that came in under their quote, how far under, in basis points. The share tells you how often the price moved; this tells you how far.

Only trades that underfilled are counted, so the figure does not get diluted by the ones that filled exactly. About 56% of settled trades match their quote to the unit.

This measure is censored, and it understates volatility exactly when volatility is highest. A fill that falls further below the quote than the caller's tolerance reverts instead of settling, so it never appears here. Read it together with the revert rate, never on its own.

The bucket has a floor of one hour. Without it the range picks a bucket of about ten minutes, and a chain that does 110 trades an hour falls under the minimum count and disappears completely. That is why ethereum was absent.

SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(block_time, $__interval), chain AS metric,
       percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (
         ORDER BY 10000.0 * (expected_amount_out - amount_out) / nullif(expected_amount_out, 0)
       ) FILTER (WHERE amount_out < expected_amount_out) AS median_shortfall_bps
FROM trades
WHERE $__timeFilter(block_time) AND tx_success AND call_success AND state_committed
  AND expected_amount_out > 0 AND amount_out IS NOT NULL AND chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE amount_out < expected_amount_out) >= 10
ORDER BY 1

panels.description:
The most recent failed calls in the selected flow, newest first.

reason is the decoded error and is usually what you want; selector alone does not separate an out-of-gas from a failed callback, and both of those arrive with no selector at all. Copy tx_hash into Router Trade Detail to see the full call.

volume_usd is empty when the pricing pipeline could not value the trade, which is common for long-tail tokens and does not itself indicate a problem.

The Watermark variable at the top selects which flow this counts. Untagged flow is never included: it is not ours and its failures say nothing about our integrations. Set the variable to a single propeller/<name> to look at one integrator.

WITH w AS (
  SELECT t.block_time, t.chain, t.tx_hash, t.msg_sender, t.token_in, t.token_out,
         t.n_hops, t.volume_usd, t.gas_used, t.router_version,
         coalesce(t.revert_selector, '(none)') AS selector,
         left(coalesce(t.revert_reason, '(no reason)'), 90) AS reason,
         CASE
           WHEN coalesce(t.watermark, '') = '' THEN '(untagged)'
           WHEN t.watermark !~* '^0x([0-9a-f]{2})+$' THEN t.watermark
           WHEN left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) = '' THEN '(untagged)'
           WHEN left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) ~ '^(66796e642f(?:3[0-9]|2e)+2f(?:3[0-9]|6[1-6]){16})'
             THEN convert_from(decode(substring(left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) from '^(66796e642f(?:3[0-9]|2e)+2f(?:3[0-9]|6[1-6]){16})'), 'hex'), 'LATIN1')
           WHEN left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)) ~ '^(2[0-9a-f]|[3-6][0-9a-f]|7[0-9a-e])+$'
             THEN convert_from(decode(left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END)), 'hex'), 'LATIN1')
           ELSE '0x' || left(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), greatest(0, length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - CASE WHEN lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)) ~ '(8021){8}$' THEN 36 + 2 * (('x' || substr(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3)), length(lower(substring(t.watermark, 3))) - 35, 2))::bit(8)::int) ELSE 0 END))
         END AS watermark
  FROM trades t
  WHERE $__timeFilter(t.block_time) AND NOT t.call_success
    AND t.chain IN (${chain:sqlstring})
)
SELECT block_time, chain, watermark, reason, selector, tx_hash,
       msg_sender, token_in, token_out, n_hops, gas_used, volume_usd, router_version
FROM w
WHERE watermark <> '(untagged)' AND watermark IN (${watermark:sqlstring})
ORDER BY block_time DESC
LIMIT 100
